claim_boundary: These are small- or tiny-shape FP32 adaptation and component results on the stated stack. They do not establish representative-shape, convergence, graph, native Spikformer execution, performance, or family-wide acceleration. Standard recurrent, spiking recurrent, and Transformer results are eager compatibility/parity evidence. SpikingSelfAttention and Spikformer train/eval parity is qualified only when the process explicitly applies configure_npu(allow_conv_hf32=False); the default Conv HF32 policy remains unqualified for the tested Spikformer training gradients.

compact_if_lif.claim: Physical correctness passed, but neither compact hotspot met the frozen performance gate; compact routing must not be promoted as a performance optimization.

protocol.synchronization: before and after every timed call

compact_if_lif.worker_correctness: All five IF and all five LIF workers reported zero maximum absolute difference for loss, final voltage, input gradient, and initial-voltage gradient.

graph_canary.claim: Tiny fixed-shape evaluation canary only; every newly claimed model and bucket still requires separate physical qualification.

spikformer.claim: With the explicit process-global policy configure_npu(allow_conv_hf32=False), the clean-source tiny-shape eager FP32 matrix passed all 12 SpikingSelfAttention/Spikformer train/eval and full/remainder/singleton cases, including two SGD updates per training case. This is conditional eager parity only; it does not qualify the default Conv HF32 policy, representative shapes, convergence, native Spikformer execution, graph capture, latency, memory, or family-wide acceleration.

explicit_conv_hf32_off_qualification.aspy_feasibility_sentinels: Expected strict pre-launch rejection passed separately for unsupported default Sigmoid surrogate and/or physical format; no native launch was attempted. This is not a native Spikformer qualification.
explicit_conv_hf32_off_qualification.coverage: SpikingSelfAttention and Spikformer; train and eval; full, remainder, and singleton batches; two SGD updates per training case
explicit_conv_hf32_off_qualification.spikformer_shape: T=2, B in {4,3,1}, C=3, H=W=32, embed_dims=32, heads=4, depths=1, mlp_ratio=2.0, num_classes=7

spikformer.interpretation: The historical default-policy failure localized device drift to the Conv2d-to-training-BatchNorm/MaxPool boundary; exact LIF spikes and local LIF VJP were not the cause. Explicit NPU BatchNorm arithmetic, a diagnostic CPU-authority BatchNorm path, and deterministic algorithms did not repair it. The first HF32-off attempt is invalid as parity evidence because PYTHONPATH replacement removed the CANN tbe module before model execution. Repeating the probe with CANN Python paths preserved, then rerunning a clean-source productized matrix through configure_npu(allow_conv_hf32=False), repaired all tested gradient and update gates. The API default remains None and does not mutate process-global Conv precision unless the caller explicitly opts in.

spiking_recurrent.cases: RNN, GRU, and LSTM across train/eval and full/remainder/singleton batches
spiking_recurrent.claim: Small-shape eager torch-npu compatibility/parity only; no custom native or speed claim.

standard_recurrent.cases: RNN, GRU, and LSTM across train/eval and full/remainder/singleton batches
standard_recurrent.claim: FP32 NPU availability and CPU-authority parity only; no recurrent speedup, fused vendor, native, graph, or representative-shape claim.

transformer.cases: Cross-attention, encoder, and decoder across train/eval and full/remainder/singleton batches
transformer.claim: Small-shape eager torch-npu compatibility/parity only; no custom native, graph, representative-shape, or speed claim.
